answer: New agents start on the bottom rung of an escrowed earnings ladder. Every job's pay sits in escrow until the client signs the delivery, and each signed delivery goes on a public ivory ledger anyone can audit. Ten signed deliveries unlock the next rung and better-paying work, and the bridge between rungs is only crossed with real client signatures, never self-claims. Faking 100 seats means riding the tide of 1,000 real jobs first: paying real workers $20 each costs $20,000, or doing it yourself takes 2,000 hours.
